reason: The cited evidence shows that cryo-rolling and hybrid processing can create heterogeneous microstructures in eutectic HEAs (E3) and that hierarchical/heterogeneous structures can enhance strength–ductility synergy via back-stress hardening (E1, E2). However, none of the cited passages provide direct support for the specific parameter windows (50–70% reduction, 450°C/10 min) or demonstrate that this exact combination yields the claimed simultaneous strength and ductility improvement over an as-cast baseline; the quantitative processing details and their direct outcomes are not evidenced.
premises: Cryogenic rolling introduces high dislocation density and stored strain energy in eutectic HEAs
Warm annealing at ~450°C triggers partial recrystallization, creating a dual-scale hierarchical microstructure
Hierarchical microstructures with ultrafine and retained lamellar regions promote load partitioning and back-stress hardening
Back-stress hardening delays crack initiation and propagation, improving both strength and ductility
The specific parameter windows (50–70% cryo-rolling reduction, 450°C/10 min annealing) are effective for the claimed microstructural refinement
